sections.heading: Formats Are a Vocabulary; Converters Are the Translator
paragraphs: Websites want WebP for speed, print wants high-resolution PNG or JPG, and email clients refuse some formats outright. Being able to [convert-image:convert image formats] on demand unblocks every pipeline.
Each format trades off differently: JPG for photographs, PNG for transparency, WebP for web efficiency. The right conversion picks the right trade-off.
ChooseTools converts images locally in the browser with quality controls that let you choose the balance.
Understanding format trade-offs saves bandwidth, preserves quality where it matters and prevents compatibility headaches when images travel between platforms.

Because conversion runs locally, even a folder of images converts quickly and nothing uploads.
The straightforward three-step process — upload, configure, download — eliminates the need for desktop software installation or command-line tools.

sections.heading: JPG, PNG, WebP: Picking the Right Output
paragraphs: JPG remains the photographic workhorse; PNG preserves transparency and text edges; WebP compresses like modern web demands.
The tool converts among them and more, applying each format's strengths correctly — no checkerboard transparency in JPG, no bloated PNG where JPG would do.
Choosing wisely at conversion time saves bytes and headaches downstream.
GIF and BMP are also supported for legacy systems and specific use cases like animated images or uncompressed archival copies.

sections.heading: Lossy vs Lossless: Choosing Compression Strategy
paragraphs: Lossy compression like JPG discards pixel data that the human eye is less likely to notice, producing smaller files at the cost of some fidelity. Lossless compression like PNG preserves every pixel exactly, resulting in larger files.

The quality slider for lossy formats lets you choose where on the spectrum between file size and visual fidelity your image should sit. A setting of 85 percent typically produces output indistinguishable from the original while reducing file size by half or more.
For images containing text, sharp edges or transparency, lossless formats prevent the artifacts and halo effects that lossy compression introduces around high-contrast boundaries.
Knowing which strategy fits the image content prevents both unnecessarily large files and visibly degraded output.

sections.heading: Transparency and Alpha Channel Handling
paragraphs: PNG supports alpha-channel transparency, allowing pixels to range from fully opaque to fully transparent. Converting a transparent PNG to JPG replaces the transparency with a solid background color, which may not be the intended result.

The converter warns or handles this transition correctly, so you can choose a background color that matches your target context rather than discovering the transparency was lost after the file is already in production.
WebP also supports alpha transparency with better compression than PNG, making it an attractive alternative for web graphics that need both transparency and small file sizes.
Understanding transparency behavior during conversion prevents the common surprise of a white or black rectangle appearing where a transparent background used to be.

sections.heading: Quality Settings That Respect Your Intent
paragraphs: Conversion isn't about maximum quality blindly; it's about the right quality for delivery context.
Adjust quality sliders so screen previews stay light while print-shares stay lossless-feeling.

Preview-oriented images benefit from aggressive compression that prioritizes load speed, while archival copies warrant minimal compression to preserve every detail for future editing.

faqs.q: Which formats can I convert between?
faqs.a: The common web and print formats are supported — including JPG, PNG and WebP — with quality controls where the format allows.
Yes. Conversion takes place entirely in your browser; your image is never uploaded to any server.

faqs.q: Can I control image quality during conversion?
faqs.a: Yes. Quality settings adjust the compression/quality balance for the target format, so you decide between size and fidelity.

faqs.q: What happens to transparency when converting to JPG?
faqs.a: JPG does not support transparency, so transparent areas are filled with a solid background color during conversion.
